_doc: RESEARCH-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-21): Ultrastable runs its own R&D department as code. An external study is ingested as data (research/studies/<id>.json): each finding names the concern, the Ultrastable mechanisms that answer it, the metric of this system that tests the answer, a target and a prediction. `python3 -m foundation research --run --apply` measures every metric from the system's own ledgers, files a Q-RES item for every finding the system does not yet meet (closing probe: the same measurement), opens and settles experiments, proposes further rule links through core/connect, and regenerates the white papers (research/papers/<id>.md, site/research-data.js, served at /research). Intake (`--intake --apply`) reads public paper feeds and files at most max_intake_items candidates a pass, perspectives with no study first. Papers state limits computed from the same data; no number in a paper is typed by hand.

questions.question: Does merging without a human review step raise the share of changes that are later reverted?
Does a change the system opens on itself reach main as fast as one a code agent session opens?
Is every deploy proven live against its own commit?
How much of the work opened is thrown away? A pull request closed without merging is rework the study would count as requested changes.
